newsitem.title: EU: EC Report Weekly Diary for Monday, June 30-Sunday, July 6.
newsitem.headline: EC Report Weekly Diary for Monday, June 30-Sunday, July 6.

text.p: HIGHLIGHTS
LUXEMBOURG - Luxembourg takes over EU presidency from Dutch. To December 31, 1997.
LUXEMBOURG - EU culture ministers meet (Mon); public hearing on future of European cultural action.
FRANKFURT - European Commission President Santer attends Monetary Institute council (Tues).
BRUSSELS - European Commission regular weekly meeting (Wed).
LUXEMBOURG - European Commission on official visit to Luxembourg followed by a n/conf on the outcome of the meeting (Thurs).
ECHTERNACH, Luxembourg - EU Employment and Social Affairs ministers hold informal meeting (Fri-Sat).
BONN - German government and European Commission sponsor European ministerial conference on "Global information networks: realising the potential" (begins at Sun).
MONDAY, JUNE 30
HAGUE - Dutch EU presidency ends. Luxembourg takes over to December 31, 1997.

LUXEMBOURG - EU culture ministers meet (1000/0800 GMT). Agenda includes public hearing on future of European cultural action (1015/0815 GMT); cross-border fixed book prices; European Cultural Cities; RAPHAEL cultural heritage programme; European fund to encourage television and film production.
BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - Dutch Agriculture Minister Jozias Van Aartsen addresses European Parliament Agriculture Committee (1500/1300 GMT).

BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - European Commissioner Marin addresses European Parliament External Economic Relations Committee on the peace process in the Mediterranean, Gulf Cooperation Council, Cuba and the Mediterranean policy (1500/1300 GMT).

BRUSSELS - Centre for European Policy Studies (CEPS) holds lunchtime meeting on "Preparing the EU for the 21st century: the Amsterdam Council and beyond" (1315/1115 GMT). Speakers include Permanent Representative of Belgium to the EU Philippe de Schoutheete. Venue: CEPS. Contact: CEPS (322) 229 3911.
TUESDAY, JULY 1
BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - European Commissioner Cresson and Federation of European Industries Chairman Oursin hold joint n/conf on financing of high technological SMEs.
FRANKFURT (NEW ITEM) - European Commission President Santer attends European Monetary Institute council.
BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - European Commissioner Fischler addresses ECOSOC Agriculture and Fisheries Section on fisheries conservation measures in the Baltic Sea (1000/0800 GMT).

BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - Luxembourg Prime Minister Jean-Claude Juncker (0900/0700 GMT) and European Investment Bank Vice-President Wolfgang Roth (1100/0900 GMT) attend European Parliament Budget Committee.
BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - European Commissioner de Silguy attends European Parliament Subcommittee on Monetary Affairs (1500/1300 GMT).

BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - European Commissioner Cresson addresses European Parliament Employment and Social Affairs Committee onn the Commission's most recent training initiatives (1600/1400 GMT) and European Commissioner Flynn addresses on the outcome of the Amsterdam European Council (1700/1500 GMT).
BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - European Parliament Civil Liberties Committee holds public hearing on the "Year against racism 1997: an interim appraisal" (0900/0700 GMT).

BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - The European Parliament and Commission conference on meat bone and meal (0930/0730 GMT) (and Wed). European Commissioner Bonino gives opening address. Main agenda includes problems concerning security of meat and bone meal; what should be done to assure the security of animal feed. Venue: Centre Borschette.
WEDNESDAY, JULY 2
BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - European Commission regular weekly meeting (0900/0700 GMT).
Provisional agenda includes:
- Preparation for meeting with Luxembourg presidency.
- Impact on the introduction of the euro on financial markets.
BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - European Parliament President Jose Maria Gil-Robles meets Spanish Bank Governor Luis Angel Rojo (0900/0700 GMT).
BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe Special Coordinator Catherine Lalumiere n/conf on Albanian elelctions (time to be confirmed).
BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - Dutch Transport Minister Annemarie Jorritsma (1500/1300 GMT).

BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - The European Parliament and Commission conference on meat bone and meal (0900/0700 GMT) (second of two days). Agenda includes: ecological and economic aspects; consumers' point of view. European Commissioner Fischler gives closing address at 1600/1400 GMT.

BRUSSELS - British Chamber of Commerce in Belgium holds lunchtime meeting on "International environmental management" (1230/1030 GMT). Venue: Sheraton Hotel. Contact: British Chamber of Commerce in Belgium by fax (322) 2305573.
THURSDAY, JULY 3
LUXEMBOURG (EXPANDED ITEM) - European Commission on official visit to Luxembourg - n/conf 1630/1430 GMT.

BRUSSELS - Centre for European Policy Studies (CEPS) holds lunchtime meeting on "The Madrid NATO summit" (1315/1115 GMT). Speaker is: Former Western European Union Secretary General Willem van Eekelen. Venue: CEPS. Contact: CEPS (322) 229 3911.
FRIDAY, JULY 4
ECHTERNACH, Luxembourg (EXPANDED ITEM) - EU Employment and Social Affairs ministers hold informal meeting (first of two days). Arrival of the delegates late afternoon. Venue: Hotel Eden du Lac.

BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - Belgian Foreign Trade Board holds conference on "Trade and investment opportunities in Venezuela's energy and petrochemical sectors" (0930/0730 GMT). Venue: World trade Centre, 163 Blvd Emile Jacqmain.
SATURDAY, JULY 5

ECHTERNACH, Luxembourg (NEW ITEM) - EU Employment and Social Affairs ministers hold informal meeting (second of two days). Informal working session begins at 0930/0730 GMT; news conference on the outcome of meeting at 1730/1530 GMT. Venue: Hotel Eden du Lac.
SUNDAY, JULY 6

BONN - German government and European Commission sponsor European ministerial conference on "Global information networks: realising the potential" (To July 8). The conference is organised in four plenary sessions: building confidence, empowering the user, making the most of content resources, creating a favourable environment for electronic commerce. The conclusions of the conference will take the form of a common ministerial declaration outlining principles governing the use of global information networks and cooperative steps in international forums.
